items.title: Palworld Teases Highly Requested Feature For Next Update
items.summary: Pocketpair teases a long-requested feature coming in Palworld
items.content:
Palworld Teases Highly Requested Feature For Next Update From GameRant (Written by Dominik Bošnjak) on September 5, 2026 | OpenCritic

The 1.1 update for Palworld will introduce a feature that players have been demanding for a while now, Pocketpair has confirmed. The catch, however, is that the developer isn’t yet ready to reveal what that feature is, though it has shared some other details about what Palworld fans can expect from the upcoming patch.

Pocketpair began publicly discussing Version 1.1 in mid-August 2026, when publishing and communications lead John "Bucky" Buckley shared a photo from a "brainstorming session" focused on the game's next major release. He also invited fans to suggest additions they wanted to see. The request, made shortly after Pocketpair released Palworld update 1.0.3 , drew around 1,700 responses within a day, prompting Buckley to clarify that ideas such as a new continent or another 20 levels were well beyond the studio's plans for Version 1.1.

If the last time you played Palworld was during Early Access, you need to unlearn these habits.

Speaking to GamesRadar+ at Gamescom 2026, Buckley revealed that one substantial addition has nevertheless made the cut. He described it as a "big specific feature" that players have been requesting "for a while," all the while declining to say what it actually is. His comments...

items.content:
Pokémon rival Palworld is attempting to lure in new players on PlayStation Plus.

Palworld , the popular Pokémon rival and open-world RPG, is free to try on PS5 right now for some PlayStation Plus subscribers. If you’ve been tempted to see what the hugely popular monster-collecting game is all about, there’s never been a better time to jump into Palworld and experience it for yourself.

Palworld , developed and published by indie studio Pocketpair, first launched in Early Access in January 2024 before officially leaving Early Access with its Version 1.0 update in July 2026.

Palworld is an open-world survival RPG that takes inspiration from Pokémon with its creature collecting, training and battling, while also incorporating crafting and survival mechanics reminiscent of games such as Minecraft . Unlike Pokémon, however, Palworld features robust online multiplayer, allowing players to team up with friends to explore, build and survive together, or turn against each other and become fierce rivals.

This week, a new PlayStation Plus Premium trial for Palworld launched , giving subscribers the perfect opportunity to try the popular survival RPG for free and decide whether it’s worth spending their hard-earned cash on.

PlayStation Plus Game Trials can vary significantly in length, with some lasting less than an hour and others offering up to five hours of gameplay. The Palworld trial sits somewhere in the middle, giving players a generous two hours to experience the full game.

During the two-hour Palworld trial, you’ll have full access to the game, can unlock trophies and, best of all, your save data will carry over to the full game if you decide to purchase it. There’s also an added incentive to take the plunge, as Palworld is currently 30% off on the PlayStation Store until September 9, 2026.

READ MORE: Pokémon rival Palworld unveils 'incredible' content update as it surpasses 40 million players

Palworld does have a story to follow, albeit a subtle one. A focus on the narrative takes a backseat, with its main emphasis being its open-world survival gameplay. Players can explore the Palpagos Islands, battle powerful bosses and uncover the mysteries surrounding the world and its Pals along the way.

In September 2024, Nintendo and The Pokémon Company sued Pocketpair, alleging that Palworld infringed several patents relating to gameplay mechanics. While the legal dispute remains ongoing, Pocketpair has since changed some of Palworld’s mechanics , including how Pals are summoned and how players can use them to glide through the world.

Claims of intellectual property infringement are always an interesting conversation, particularly in an industry where games have been building upon existing ideas for decades.

Pokémon itself has often been compared to Dragon Quest, with Dragon Quest V's monster-recruitment system frequently cited as an influence on Pokémon's creature-collecting concept. Meanwhile, Akira Toriyama's distinctive artwork for Dragon Quest has also been noted as an influence on the visual style of early Pokémon artwork.

Palworld is out now on PC, PlayStation and Xbox.

In case you don't know about Craftopia yourself, it's an open-world anime-style survival game that's been in limbo for… well, ever since its Early Access release over on Steam on September 4 back in 2020. It's gotten some minor updates – and, honestly, I mean pretty dang minor, considering the timeline – here and there, but those of us with the game in our library have waited for a 1.0 launch for what feels like forever now.

And, thankfully, it's finally coming – and with it, hopefully some more positive reviews, too, seeing as it's got a "Mostly Negative" rating as it stands (yes, much of the feedback cites the game being "unfinished" and dubs Craftopia an "abandoned" title from Pocketpair). As a new update from the developers reads, "Craftopia will leave Early Access and release into Version 1.0 in 2027." What's another few months of waiting, eh?

Happy birthday to Craftopia, the game that Pocketpair would not exist without! Today, we have news about the long-awaited 1.0 for Craftopia, as well as news about Xbox and the anniversary update! Please check out the post below! https://t.co/UQcHcVANoA September 4, 2026

With 1.0, Pocketpair says to expect "cleaning up and refining the existing experience, addressing outstanding issues, and making Craftopia as enjoyable and polished as possible for its full release" rather than "sheer content volume as some players might expect" – but, "there will still be new content arriving." It's exciting, even if it's more minor than some would hope in terms of content, and the devs seem to think so as well.

Head of Pocketpair publishing and communications John "Bucky" Buckley responds to the news himself on X , writing, "Happy birthday to Craftopia, the game that Pocketpair would not exist without!" He also teases the Xbox release of the old survival gem, which is similarly set for 2027. I'm intrigued to see the devs acknowledge their origins in Craftopia myself, personally, and as a player, too, I'm thrilled it's finally releasing.

Palworld 1.0 sees the game's biggest Steam player spike since its massive early access launch Palworld 1.0 briefly overtook king of Steam Counter-Strike 2, and devs are basking in the victory Palworld 1.0 sounds massive as lead teases "27 pdf pages" of patch notes coming to the game Here's hoping that Craftopia 1.0 delivers on its promises to clean up the admittedly janky (at times, anyway) open-world game and also add a little bit of new content to it. I know I'll be looking forward to the release next year.

items.content:
Garena announced on the 2nd that it has opened domestic pre-registration for the mobile multiplayer RPG 'Palworld Online'.

'Palworld Online' is a new title developed and published by Garena based on an official license from Japanese game developer Pocketpair. It utilizes the 'Palworld' IP, which has accumulated over 40 million players worldwide, and is scheduled to launch first globally in Korea in 2026.

The game is designed around player cooperation and shared growth. It features cooperative Pal-capturing gameplay, PvE content, PvP combat, and shared base management. Core elements of the original title—such as Pal collecting, survival, crafting, and open-world exploration—have also been implemented in a seamless online world tailored for mobile environments.

Players can explore the open world with other players, build structures, and engage in combat.

Pre-registration is available on Google Play and the Apple App Store. Depending on the number of participants, rewards such as 50,000 Gold Coins, 20 Training Manuals (M), 50 Dog Coins, a Huge Verdant Egg, and 10 Tera Spheres will be distributed, while rewards for all pre-registered users will be revealed at a later date.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

Chris Reed is a commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

items.title: Palworld 1.0 Review – Bigger, Better, and Still Brutally Addictive
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 is crammed with new content. More Pals, better quests, and a fully realized world for new and returning players to explore.
items.content:
Remember Palworld ? Well, the controversial game from Pocketpair finally has a 1.0 release. After two years, this feels like a very different animal than the one I initially encountered. The quest system is more complete, the UI is polished, and the world feels much more interconnected than before. While there are still some rough edges, this version of Palworld is a vastly improved one.

Now, I haven’t been keeping up with every iteration of Palworld released up to this point. So I’m not clear on how gradual or sudden these changes might be. But oh man, the quest system feels like night and day. You’re fed a steady stream of quests from the jump. They pair nicely with the tech tree, they appear on your map, and they sync with your compass. Yes, this is incredibly basic stuff. We figured out quest design decades ago. But you really appreciate the elegance of that design when it’s missing. Then when it finally shows up? It’s water in the desert.

Beyond the quests, it turns out Palworld works much better with connective tissue in place. Fast travel points, side quests, a detailed map, and distant objectives (like a floating island on the horizon) all make the world feel more tangible. Having an objective at all times kept me hooked on the game. Or at least, objectives are perfect for stringing you along until the factory sim element gets its claws in you. Once the big machine gets going, you don’t need anything else to maintain momentum.

The complete list of additions in Palworld 1.0 is downright intimidating. You can read the whole thing on their Steam page, but the highlights are remarkable. 72 new Pals, the Sunreach region, the World Tree, and an increased level cap all speak to a much larger, more complete game. There’s more of course, but the point remains – Palworld has undergone significant changes since the early access days.

This new version of Palworld still has some flaws, to be fair. The laptop I’m using is decently powerful, but I encountered a handful of framerate dips regardless. More important than the tiny performance issues is the core gameplay loop. Things hum along at a more relatable pace than ever before, sure. But you’re still faced with a pretty murderous grind. Pal levels creep upward slowly, and getting through that tech trees gets daunting quite quickly. While things start out breezy enough, the endgame is strictly for simulation psychopaths.

By which I mean the truly dedicated. Which is totally fine! There’s a fascinating disconnect between the monster battling and the base building. You can immerse yourself in one and ignore the other, at least for a hefty chunk of playtime. Although perhaps my impressions of the battling are skewed by hands off it all is. Your Pals run on autopilot, both in battle and beyond it. So for me, the fights are a diversion from my tiny empire.

In that regard, Palworld remains a specialized interest. Either you’re ready to get lost in the details of empire expansion and monster murder, or you’ll quickly lose momentum. The quest system, new content, and expanded Pal roster are all incidental in the face of this essential truth. The gooey caramel center that is the gameplay loop is more or less the same as it ever was. My mind was changed about this game, true. But I’m prone to hyper focus and bouts of mania. So a vast and ruthless machine like Palworld is straight up catnip for my badly wired brain.

The 1.0 release of Palworld presents a very different game than the original early access version. The quest system has been revamped, the map has been expanded, and civilization is scattered everywhere. But the gameplay loop is still pretty relentless. Plus, the rough edges haven’t been completely removed. If the old game was almost it for you, this new iteration might be exactly what you yearned for. But Palworld 1.0 is still an acquired taste.

***A Steam key was provided by the publisher***
